newsitem.title: USA: Teleport to buy CERFnet Internet firm for $66.4 million.
newsitem.headline: Teleport to buy CERFnet Internet firm for $66.4 million.

text.p: Teleport Communications Group Inc., which is owned by a group of cable TV companies, said Monday it would buy Internet service provider CERFnet from General Atomics and its affiliates in a stock deal worth $66.4 million.

Under the deal, Teleport will acquire General Atomics in exchange for 2.1 million of its class 'A' common shares. Based on Teleport's closing price Friday of $31.625, the deal is valued at $66.4 million.
General Atomics is a founding participant in the National Science Foundation Network, which later evolved into the Internet.
CERFnet, based in San Diego, is one of the oldest Internet providers, having been set up in 1989. It has 6,000 mainly corporate and professional users.

"TCG will provide CERFnet's customer base with sophisticated telecommunication services, while CERFnet will provide TCG's customer base with equally high-quality Internet service," Teleport chief executive Robert Annunziata said.
Teleport's stock was unchanged at $31.625 on Nasdaq.
